forest: Scattered groves and gallery-woods of oak and willow along the streams of the wide southern grasslands, islands of shade among the horse-pastures of the Eothraim. Open, sunlit, and loud with wind over grass.
road: A grass-worn horse-track across the open plains, faint but sure to those who ride it, following the streams and the herds rather than any surveyor's line.
trail: A rider's thread across the grass, barely there, that follows the graze of the herds and the line of the streams.
plains: Broad northern grasslands stretching flat to the sky, rich pasture in summer and mire in the spring thaw, loud always with wind over grass.

forest: Sparse, hardy woods of pine and birch in a rugged northern wilderland, wind-bitten and thinly grown over stony ground. A frontier forest, cold and little-trodden.
road: A rough track between scattered northern steads, mud in the thaw and dust in the summer, kept open only by the passing of the folk who need it.
trail: A muddy footpath between northern crofts, faint and rough, marked by a leaning post or a cairn where it forks.
plains: Open rough plains of coarse grass and reed between the streams, half-wild and thinly grazed under a wide grey sky.

forest: The black heart of the Wood — ancient oaks and beeches bent together into a gloomy arch, trunks tangled with ivy and lichen. Beneath them a dim green light barely reveals the way; the air is thick, still and watchful, and black butterflies drift through the gloom like leaves that will not fall.
road: The Elf-path winds east under the eaves — a narrow thread of beaten earth between black trunks. It is the one safe way through, and straying from it is the forest's oldest trap.
trail: Within the wood the game-trails are lies — they wind among the roots and fade in the dark. The stream that crosses them runs black and still, and it is not to be touched.

forest: The north-eaves of the Wood — greener and less shadowed than the south, beech-woods over halls of living stone where the Elvenking holds his court beneath the hill.
road: The Forest River runs out of the black woods to the gates of the Elvenking's halls; the road crosses it on a bridge of stone, and beyond the doors there is no road but the river.
trail: Hidden ways thread the green wood to the halls and the deep cellars; the forest here is watched and warded, and the deer-parks are ancient.

forest: Groves of oak and beech clothe the lower slopes — a fair field of trees above the grassland, green in spring and russet after the turning.
hill: Rolling downs above the Anduin vales — turf thick underfoot and grave-mounds green where older folk sleep under the grass.
mountains_low: The southern spurs of the Misty Mountains fall away in grey ridges toward the field, their feet clothed in dark pine.
mountains_med: High shoulders of the range look down on the field; on clear days the snow on the far peaks burns white against the sky.
mountains_high: The cold crowns of the world stand beyond the dale — close enough to touch the sight though far to reach, remote and bright.
road: The old road of the North Kingdom runs through the field — its line still clear under the grass, marking where an army once broke and a realm was lost.
trail: Green trails cross the field between the groves; the grass is soft underfoot and the larks are loud in the high air.

forest: Cultivated, Mediterranean woodland: groves of holm-oak, chestnut and cypress give way to olive and almond on the warmer slopes, with orchards and flowering vales. The undergrowth is aromatic with broom, thyme and rockrose; tended, sunlit, prosperous woods.
hill: Fertile foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with vine and olive and laced with clear streams. Warm and sunlit, the green skirts where mountain meets tilled land.
road: A well-kept Gondorian road of fitted stone, straight and sure, with drainage and standing waymarks; the traffic of trade and soldiery keeps it busy and its verges clear.
trail: A trodden countryside path between orchards and terraces, sun-warm and clear, worn smooth by shepherds and farmhands.
plains: Dry southern steppe of bleached grass and thornscrub, shimmering with heat, rolling flat and vast toward the unknown east.

forest: The woods of Anorien are the tended groves of the north — planted beech and fir on the foothills of the White Mountains, cut and grown again for the City's timber. Eastward the old Drúadan Forest stands wild and dark on the mountain's knees.
hill: The beacon-hills march along the mountain feet — Amon Dîn, Eilenach, Nardol, Erelas, Min-Rimmon, Calenhad, and green Halifirien last and highest. Below them the land rolls down in long open slopes to the fields of the Pelennor.
mountains_low: The foothills of Ered Nimrais rise steep above the plain — grass slopes and pine-woods under the white wall, where snow lingers late and cold streams run down out of the heights.
mountains_med: The White Mountains fill the southern sky — a rampart of grey cliff and snowfield, Mindolluin nearest and tallest over the City. The wind that comes down off them at evening smells of stone and ice.
mountains_high: High and remote the great peaks stand in their snows; even at midsummer the air off them is cool, and they catch the first and last light like a row of lit beacons.
road: The Great West Road runs from the City through the green townlands and away north toward the fords of the Isen and the fields of the Mark. Its stones are worn by hooves and by the passage of armies.
trail: Drove-roads and field-paths cross the farms; on the foothills the old paths of the mountain-men climb through the fir-woods to the beacon-tops.
plains: The Pelennor is a fenced green field between mountain and river — dykes and orchards, tilth and meadow, all within sight of the City walls. Beyond the wall the land rises into the fair empty hills of the north.

forest: Scrub and thorn where anything grows at all — blackened clumps and dead brakes, the wreck of a burned land. The few living trees stand like scarecrows at the field's edge.
marshes: The Dead Marshes — a wide drowned waste of meres and reed-beds strewn with the wreck of a great battle. Faint lights move over the pools at night, and pale faces look up through the green water, cold and still.
road: Three pale dusty roads converge upon the Black Gate — one bending north, one lost eastward in the mists under Ered Lithui, and one winding through a narrow defile of the hills.
trail: Paths through the fens are few and treacherous; the firm ways are old causeways half-drowned, and the ground gurgles underfoot and slides.
plains: The battle-plain itself — cracked earth, dry reeking mounds and slag-pits where no grass grows. The wind drives dust over the old dead, and nothing here is at rest.

forest: A dark forest of ancient pines on the mountain's feet — close-grown, silent, and very old. The Wild Men move here unseen, and the wood keeps its secrets; the trees remember the first men who walked under them.
road: The old Stonewain Road winds through the forest — a sunken way of grey slabs laid by forgotten hands to carry stone to the City. It is half-lost under moss and the roots of pines.
trail: Narrow trails thread the dark aisles of the wood, known only to the folk of the trees. The forest is a maze where the markers are carved stones that seem to watch.

forest: Wooded shores ring the Long Lake — pine on the steep mountain flanks and willow on the wet margins; the trees of Mirkwood's eaves come down to the water's edge.
road: The ways of Esgaroth are waterways — the channels between the lake's long arms and the current of the Forest River, spanned by the wooden streets and piers of Lake-town.
trail: On land, marshy paths skirt the lake's southern arms; on the water the ways are marked by piles and lanterns between the hidden channels.

forest: Cultivated, Mediterranean woodland: groves of holm-oak, chestnut and cypress give way to olive and almond on the warmer slopes, with orchards and flowering vales. The undergrowth is aromatic with broom, thyme and rockrose; tended, sunlit, prosperous woods.
hill: Fertile foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with vine and olive and laced with clear streams. Warm and sunlit, the green skirts where mountain meets tilled land.
mountains_low: The green foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with olive and vine where they meet the lowlands, laced with shepherd-paths and tumbling brooks. Warm, fertile and sunlit, the gentlest face of the great range.
mountains_med: The middle slopes of the Ered Nimrais, where forest yields to alpine meadow and grey crag. Cloud snags on the ridges, streams fall in white threads, and the air thins and chills as the green runs out into stone.
mountains_high: The high White Mountains, the Ered Nimrais, crowned with perpetual snow and glacier above the treeline. Knife-edged ridges and sheer pale walls blaze in the sun; the cold is absolute, the silence broken only by wind and distant ice.
road: A well-kept Gondorian road of fitted stone, straight and sure, with drainage and standing waymarks; the traffic of trade and soldiery keeps it busy and its verges clear.
trail: A trodden countryside path between orchards and terraces, sun-warm and clear, worn smooth by shepherds and farmhands.
plains: The rich level fields of Gondor's most peopled land, watered by many rivers, quilted with farms and pasture between the coast and the hills.

forest: Sun-scorched scrubland rather than true forest: thorn, tamarisk and stunted wind-bitten oak scattered over an arid contested plateau, their roots gripping cracked red earth. Sparse, dusty shade in a debated borderland baked between Gondor and the South.
hill: Fertile foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with vine and olive and laced with clear streams. Warm and sunlit, the green skirts where mountain meets tilled land.
road: A well-kept Gondorian road of fitted stone, straight and sure, with drainage and standing waymarks; the traffic of trade and soldiery keeps it busy and its verges clear.
trail: A trodden countryside path between orchards and terraces, sun-warm and clear, worn smooth by shepherds and farmhands.
plains: Sun-baked open country of dune-field, dry scrub and salt-flat, shimmering and stark, rolling toward the deserts of the south.

forest: Sparse, wind-scoured woods on a rocky, desolate coast: stunted oak and pine bent by the sea-gales, clinging to the spurs of the White Mountains above fishing villages and gold-miners' tracks. Few trees of size survive here; the land is harsh, salt-bitten and poor, far from Gondor's prosperous heartland.

forest: Cool northern woods of birch, rowan and Scots pine over stony, heather-fringed soil, with stands of old oak in the sheltered hollows. Clean-aired and quiet, the groves of a fading Dunedain land where ruined walls surface among the roots.
hill: Rolling green-grey downs of cropped turf and gorse, strewn with standing stones and grass-grown barrows, mist clinging low at dawn. The bones of old Arnor, walls, cairns, weather-worn towers, surface across the lonely heights.
marshes: The Midgewater Marshes: low sodden ground of shallow pools, reeds and clinging mud, plagued by clouds of midges and a ceaseless nightly croaking. Wet, wearying misery rather than true peril.
road: An old Dunadan road, its worn paving-stones still true beneath the turf, running between friendly farms and waystones; a safe and travelled way where a cart or a rider is no rare sight.
trail: A pleasant footpath winding over green downs, firm and dry underfoot, dipping between hedgerows where blackberries grow and a farm chimney is never far off.

forest: A mixed land more than a wood: fertile lowland plains and pasture broken by ragged copses of oak and birch, the thinned remnant of older forest. Harsh winds scour the uplands while the river-vales lie green and tilled, dotted with the heath and bracken reclaiming abandoned ground.
hill: Low chalk-and-turf downs rolling to the horizon, dotted with ancient barrows and crowned here and there by weathered stone. Open, windswept, and brooding over the old graves.
road: A weathered stretch of the Great North Road, once proud and now patched and rutted, its milestones toppled; still used by merchant caravans that move in numbers, wary of the empty leagues between towns.
trail: A faint field-path through heath and old pasture, easy to lose where the bracken has swallowed it, threading between grass-grown barrows.
plains: Wide degraded lowlands of heath and rough pasture, the felled and half-empty plain where great forest once stood, rolling flat toward the sea.

forest: Dark, storm-twisted oakwood clinging to a wind-scoured coastal cape, dense and salt-bitten, sheltering an ancient folk apart from the world. A brooding, silent wood under sea-grey skies.
road: No road worth the name; only a treacherous trace through the dark wood and its poisoned mires, known to the Woses and shunned by all others.
trail: A perilous thread through the twisted wood, marked by Wose-signs a stranger cannot read, skirting the mires where worse things wait.

forest: Woods of resinous fir, cedar and cypress clothe the broken hills, set among broad glades where herbs and heath grow thick. The air is fresh and sweet, and recalls fairer countries far to the north.
hill: Green broken hills rolling down toward the Anduin — a fair land gone half-wild, where old gorse blooms gold on the scarred slopes and bay, thyme and sage fill the hollows with scent.
road: The old South Road winds down toward the cross-roads and the ruined bridges of Osgiliath — grass-grown now, and shadowed where it nears the eastern vale.
trail: Hidden paths thread the thicket and the glade — the ways of rangers among the gorse and myrtle, running to lookouts above the river and the forbidden pools.

forest: The dark fir-wood of the Dimholt clings to the mountain's root — black trees that seem untouched by light, where old stones stand in rows like sentinels before a hidden door.
hill: Green upland pastures above the Morthond vale, falling away in steep grassy slopes to the black river below. The southern cliffs rise sheer beyond, like a wall of stone.
mountains_low: The foothills of the White Mountains rise in long grassy spurs; sheep-paths wind among gorse and stone, and the high flocks graze where the air thins.
mountains_med: The southern wall of Ered Nimrais towers over the vale — white peaks above the black wood of Dimholt and the dark door that no foot returns from.
mountains_high: The high snows stand remote and bright; at their feet the mountain's shadow fills the upper vale through most of the day, and the cold comes down before the light goes.
road: The road runs up the vale beside the black water of the Morthond, passing under the shadow of the cliffs to the mountain hamlets and the high stone circles of the old folk.
trail: Old paths climb the grass slopes to the high pastures; one darker track enters the Dimholt and ends at the upright stone like a warning finger, and beyond it there is no path.

forest: Sparse degraded woods of oak and thorn on a windswept plateau, the felled and grazed-over remnant of older forest. Heath and bracken reclaim the gaps; bleak and half-empty.
road: A lonely stretch of old road across the windswept plateau, its paving long since scattered, running empty between distant and half-ruined steads.
trail: A lonely path across the empty plateau, faint in the wind-flattened grass, marked by the odd standing stone worn faceless.
plains: A bleak windswept plateau of wind-flattened grass and empty distance, half-wild and all but unpeopled beneath a wide sky.

forest: Cold Elvish woods of the far north-west: wind-bent oak, downy birch and dark pine on stony slopes that fall toward the sea, the canopy sculpted low by salt gales. Deep fern and moss below, the light falling grey and silver in groves grown ancient and still.
road: A quiet coastal track of grey stone laid by the Elves long ago, little used now, running between scattered havens above the sea-cliffs.
trail: A faint cliff-path above the sea, salt-grass to either side, dipping to hidden coves and easily missed in the mist.

forest: Stunted pine and birch clinging to dark, ore-streaked slopes, sparse and hardy. The wood gives out fast into rugged dwarf-mined stone; the air smells of iron and cold.
hill: Low rugged ridges of dark ore-bearing stone, scarred with dwarf-mines and old roads, hard and treeless and smelling of iron.
mountains_low: The lower slopes of the Iron Hills, dark with ore-bearing rock and dwarf-delvings, ridged and rugged but not lofty, the wind smelling of iron and cold stone.
road: A hard dwarf-road of dressed stone, straight and enduring, cut for ore-wagons between the delvings, ringing under iron-shod wheels.
trail: A stony miner's path between the delvings, blazed with chisel-marks on the rock, hard and sure though never gentle.

forest: Woodlands of pine and rowan clothe the lower valley — young growth on old burnt land, where the Desolation of the Dragon once spread grey ash for miles around the Mountain.
road: The road runs up the long valley to the Front Gate of Erebor beside the River Running — a way remade and busy again, where the realm of the dwarves and the town of Dale keep their watch and their trade.
trail: Paths climb the bare slopes about the Mountain — stony ways where the old scars of the desolation are still carved in the rock, and the raven-guards watch from the bare ridge of Ravenhill.

forest: Quiet green coastal woods of oak, hazel, holly and alder along the southern Gulf of Lhun, mild and sheltered. Ferny, mossy understory, dappled sea-light, and the lingering peace of an Elvish land at the world's western edge.
road: A mild green road along the southern shore, Elf-laid and enduring, running between serene estates where few travellers ever pass.
trail: A gentle wooded path along the shore, mild and green, wandering between quiet Elven dwellings half-hidden in the trees.

forest: On the seaward slopes the woods of Lindon stand — tall pines and green oakwoods that have stood since the Elder Days, the last living margin of a land the Sea drowned.
mountains_low: The Blue Mountains rise in grey-blue ridges from the green coast — old, worn heights split by the Gulf of Lhûn where the Sea comes far inland.
mountains_med: The high moors and shoulders of the range are bare and wind-scoured; the stone is blue slate, and the snow lies on it late into spring.
road: The road to the Grey Havens runs west along the gulf — a white way ending at the quays where the swan-prowed ships wait for the last sailing.
trail: Old dwarf-roads and elven paths thread the valleys of the range — ways worn before the world was changed, still trodden by the dwindling folk of the mountains' halls.

trail: A gentle wooded path along the shore, mild and green, wandering between quiet Elven dwellings half-hidden in the trees.

road: The great seaways of Belegaer run grey and wide under the western sky — the long lanes out of the Havens, where the swan-prowed ships take their leave of the shores of Middle-earth.
trail: The lesser lanes of the coast-wise sailors wind between cape and island, marked by the lights of the Havens and the wheeling of white sea-birds.

mountains_low: The lower skirts of the Blue Mountains: rounded heather-clad shoulders of grey stone rising from the pinewoods, cut by cold streams and silent old dwarf-roads. Steep but never deadly, the air sharp with resin and sea-wind.
mountains_med: The middle heights of the Blue Mountains, bare rock breaking through the heath, wind singing in the gullies. Old delvings and the rubble of vanished dwarf-mansions scar the scree-slopes, and the cold bites even in summer.
road: A mild green road along the southern shore, Elf-laid and enduring, running between serene estates where few travellers ever pass.
trail: A gentle wooded path along the shore, mild and green, wandering between quiet Elven dwellings half-hidden in the trees.

forest: Wooded shores and willow-islands crowd the River's banks; upstream the shores grow steep, and trees stand dark along the narrowing channel where the current quickens.
marshes: Long fenlands fringe the low western banks — reeds and sad grasses where small birds pipe and whistle, and swan-wings rush overhead at dusk.
road: The River itself is the road — a broad grey flood running south between the banks, misty at dawn and hiding the far shore. Below the rapids of Sarn Gebir the way is broken and the portage steep.
trail: Landing-paths of trodden mud and reed thread the banks; above them stony shores rise toward wooded hills and bare uplands of grey rock.
plains: Open grasslands roll back from the western bank — treeless plains where a fresh breeze brings thin clouds up from the distant south, and shadows lengthen slowly at day's end.

forest: Wooded slopes climb from the lake-shore at the field of the green lawns — groves of rowan and oak beneath the heights, where a small spring rises and falls beside the grey water.
marshes: Southward the land breaks into tangled fens before the marshes of the dead — a wilderness of reeds, pools and boggy ground, drear and unkind under a low sky.
road: The River below the Falls is the way south — but the way is broken by the rapids of Sarn Gebir and the great fall of Rauros, and the portage is steep and stony.
trail: Old paths climb from the lawns to the high seats of the hills — worn stone steps split by tree-roots, where the watchers of Gondor once looked east across the water.

forest: The west-eaves of the great Wood — oak and elm under the shadow of the deeper forest, friendlier than the black heart but still dim and watchful. The Woodmen's halls stand in clearings hidden among them.
road: The forest-roads of the Woodmen run between hidden halls and the western fords of Anduin — narrow ways kept secret from the dark things of the Wood.
trail: Paths thread the oak-woods between the clearings; red deer move on them, and the Woodmen know each mark and turning as their own hall.

forest: Great oaks and elms clothe the vales between river and mountain — the woodlands of the Beornings, deep in mast and honey, where the deer and the bees have more right than any stranger.
marshes: Reed-beds and fen-pools spread where the streams leave the mountains — the Gladden Fields, quiet under the sky and whispering of a doom long past.
road: The Old Ford and the paths of the forest road make the way; the River runs broad between the banks, and the mountains wall the west.
trail: Trails climb from the fords to the Carrock — the great stone standing mid-river — and wind on into the vales under the eaves of the Wood.

mountains_low: Steep, deceptive slopes of pine and bare rock where the high country begins. Wind, falling water, and cracking stone break the mountain silence, and the paths lie as often as they lead.
mountains_med: Grey shoulders and hanging valleys between the snow-line and the woods; waterfalls leap from the cliffs and vanish into mist below, and the passes are ledges of cold stone.
mountains_high: The high peaks stand above a world of cloud — cruel Caradhras, Celebdil's bare horn, and Fanuidhol's grey head. Thunder and lightning break over them when the mountains are angry, and ice falls like rain.
road: The high passes climb by exposed ledges and false paths; at the crest the way narrows to a knife of stone between storms, and the Redhorn Gate keeps its own grim weather.
trail: Goat-paths thread the crags; below them the valleys open in glimpses of green between the pines, and the mountains cast long shadows at sunset across the hidden dales.

forest: Green hills crowned with woods of tall trees; on their highest ridge the white towers of Elostirion stand — the last westward look of the Elves before the Sea.
road: The East Road runs on through the hills toward the Sea; beyond them lie the Grey Havens, and the way west ends at the world's edge.
trail: Quiet paths climb the green ridges to the white towers; from their heights a far eye might glimpse the Sea itself on the clearest days.

forest: Grim, broken upland woods of stunted oak, pine and thorn strewn with mossy boulders, cold and ill-tended. In the Trollshaws and Ettenmoors the trees shelter trolls and worse among the tumbled grey stones.
hill: Bleak boulder-strewn moor-hills of grey rock and coarse grass, cold and trackless, where trolls den among the tumbled stones and the wind moans across empty heights.
road: A broken remnant of an old Dunadan road, its stones heaved apart by frost and root, half-reclaimed by heather; a grim and little-mended way where travellers are watched from the hills.
trail: Barely a trail at all, a lost thread through the black-pine hollows, marked only by old blazes cut in the bark and half healed over by time.

forest: Thick woods of beech and oak cover the broken ground, dim even at noon. The shade is old and uneasy; travellers speak low here without knowing why.
hill: Steep stony hills folded into ravines and hollows — troll-country, where the caves in the rock are best left unsearched and the fires seen among the trees at night are best left alone.
road: The Road climbs and winds among the hills, fording stony streams that rush down noisy and cold from the mountains; its verges are grown over and the land remembers crueller times.
trail: Stony paths wind downhill beside rock walls, dropping into bush-filled hollows on the far side; every turn demands a pause and a listening.

forest: Stunted, wind-broken pine and thorn cling to cold grey slopes under perpetual cloud, snow lingering in their shadow. A grim, sparse wood in a land that resents the living.
hill: Cold bare hill-country under perpetual grey cloud, snow lingering in the hollows, grim and silent beneath the brooding strongholds of the Witch-king.
mountains_low: The cold low mountains of Angmar, bare grey rock under perpetual cloud, snow-streaked and wind-scoured, where the Witch-king's strongholds brood among the crags.
road: A hard-frozen war-road of grey stone kept open by slave-gangs, rutted by the passage of the Witch-king's supply caravans, watched from cold forts along its length.
trail: A frozen track over bare grey slopes, marked by the odd heap of stones, treacherous with ice and easily lost when the cloud comes down.

forest: On the seaward slopes the woods of Lindon stand — tall pines and green oakwoods that have stood since the Elder Days, the last living margin of a land the Sea drowned.
mountains_low: The Blue Mountains rise in grey-blue ridges from the green coast — old, worn heights split by the Gulf of Lhûn where the Sea comes far inland.
mountains_med: The high moors and shoulders of the range are bare and wind-scoured; the stone is blue slate, and the snow lies on it late into spring.
road: The road to the Grey Havens runs west along the gulf — a white way ending at the quays where the swan-prowed ships wait for the last sailing.
trail: Old dwarf-roads and elven paths thread the valleys of the range — ways worn before the world was changed, still trodden by the dwindling folk of the mountains' halls.

forest: Cold Elvish woods of the far north-west: wind-bent oak, downy birch and dark pine on stony slopes that fall toward the sea, the canopy sculpted low by salt gales. Deep fern and moss below, the light falling grey and silver in groves grown ancient and still.
road: A quiet coastal track of grey stone laid by the Elves long ago, little used now, running between scattered havens above the sea-cliffs.
trail: A faint cliff-path above the sea, salt-grass to either side, dipping to hidden coves and easily missed in the mist.

forest: Cool northern woods of birch, rowan and Scots pine over stony, heather-fringed soil, with stands of old oak in the sheltered hollows. Clean-aired and quiet, the groves of a fading Dunedain land where ruined walls surface among the roots.
hill: Rolling green-grey downs of cropped turf and gorse, strewn with standing stones and grass-grown barrows, mist clinging low at dawn. The bones of old Arnor, walls, cairns, weather-worn towers, surface across the lonely heights.
marshes: The Midgewater Marshes: low sodden ground of shallow pools, reeds and clinging mud, plagued by clouds of midges and a ceaseless nightly croaking. Wet, wearying misery rather than true peril.
road: An old Dunadan road, its worn paving-stones still true beneath the turf, running between friendly farms and waystones; a safe and travelled way where a cart or a rider is no rare sight.
trail: A pleasant footpath winding over green downs, firm and dry underfoot, dipping between hedgerows where blackberries grow and a farm chimney is never far off.

forest: A wall of ancient trees — oak and ash and gnarled willow grown so close that daylight fails among them. The air is still and watchful; moisture drips without wind, and a shout returns muffled, with no answer.
road: No true road runs under the eaves — only the old paths that the Forest tolerates, narrow ways that shift and fade between one visit and the next.
trail: The paths wind among huge roots and fallen boughs, doubling back as if the wood itself misdirected the feet. In the deep dells a stream murmurs over wild herbs, and the willows creak and rustle though no wind stirs.

forest: A mixed land more than a wood: fertile lowland plains and pasture broken by ragged copses of oak and birch, the thinned remnant of older forest. Harsh winds scour the uplands while the river-vales lie green and tilled, dotted with the heath and bracken reclaiming abandoned ground.
hill: Low chalk-and-turf downs rolling to the horizon, dotted with ancient barrows and crowned here and there by weathered stone. Open, windswept, and brooding over the old graves.
road: A weathered stretch of the Great North Road, once proud and now patched and rutted, its milestones toppled; still used by merchant caravans that move in numbers, wary of the empty leagues between towns.
trail: A faint field-path through heath and old pasture, easy to lose where the bracken has swallowed it, threading between grass-grown barrows.

forest: Scrub and stunted trees grow in dense patches between barren spaces — hawthorn, briar and wind-bent ash. In the thickets grows kingsfoil, sweetening the air where a leaf is crushed.
hill: A long line of ancient hills marching north and south, crowned here and there with the ringed ruins of old watch-towers. Weathertop stands highest — bare, windy, and commanding all the Road below.
marshes: In the low ground east of the ridge the Midgewater Marshes stretch flat and reedy — pools, sedge, and the cries of hidden birds under a wide grey sky.
road: The East Road runs along the western feet of the hills — the last true way before the wild. From the ridges it shows pale and lonely under the sky.
trail: Faint paths thread the heather and stone of the heights, made more by sheep and weather than by feet; south of the Road the ground is trackless scrub and thicket.

forest: The woodlands of the Mark are the eaves of Fangorn's skirts on the north and dark fir in the mountain dales; the Westfold's groves are windbreaks of beech on the farms.
mountains_low: The foothills of the White Mountains rise steep and green behind Edoras — long grass slopes where the horse-herds graze beneath the high white wall.
mountains_med: The Ered Nimrais make the southern wall of the Mark — a white rampart from Dunharrow to the Isen, with the deep green gorge of Harrowdale cleft into their feet.
mountains_high: The high snows stand over the Mark like a second sky — Starkhorn and Irensaga and the Dwimorberg, the haunted peak where the Dark Door waits in the mountain's root.
road: The roads of the Mark are green ways beaten by hooves — the road to Edoras under its green hill, and the west road running along the mountain wall toward the Fords of Isen.
trail: Horse-paths cross the open grass in every direction; in the dales the tracks climb beside rushing streams to the high pastures and the hidden refuges.
plains: The Riddermark — a sea of grass from the Entwash to the mountain wall, empty and wide under a huge sky. The wind never rests on it, and the distant riders are small as dust.

forest: Sparse woods of birch and thorn stand on the northern slopes; toward the east the great dark line of Fangorn's eaves marks the land's end.
road: No true roads cross the Wold — only the green tracks of the Riders going north to the downs, and the old path toward the Fords of the Entwash.
trail: Grass tracks wind over the rolling uplands; eastward they fade where the dark forest begins and the land falls away to the Entwash's banks.
plains: The Wold is a high rolling grassland — lonelier and wilder than the fields of the south, empty downs where the northern herds graze and the wind has the run of the sky.

forest: Cold, sparse stands of hardy pine and birch on the bleak northern skirts of Gundabad, wind-stripped and snow-streaked, thinning fast into bare rock.
mountains_low: The lower skirts of Mount Gundabad, bare grey stone and tundra-grass swept by an endless cold wind, snow lingering in the hollows of a grim orc-haunted height.
road: A harsh orc-trodden way through the cold northern uplands below Gundabad, unpaved and menacing, kept by the enemy rather than by any free folk.
trail: A harsh trace over cold stone below Gundabad, orc-trodden and mean, that gives out among the boulders.

forest: At the edge of the Plain of Everlasting Cold, only dwarf-birch and creeping pine survive in sheltered hollows before the tundra takes all. Frost-stunted and sparse under a wide pale sky.
road: No made road; a bleak route across the frozen plain marked by rare cairns, swept bare by the wind and lost under drifting snow.
trail: A faint line across the frozen plain, read from drift and cairn, that the next wind will scour away.

mountains_low: The forest edge climbs into broken foothills of pine and scree; above them the bare rock rises in walls and chimneys toward the passes.
mountains_med: High grey slopes where the great eagles have their eyries, looking down over oak and elm woods and the River winding far below.
mountains_high: The great peaks of the north — bare stone and permanent snow, cleft by the passes where the paths go in and do not all come out. The goblins' doors are hidden in the rocks.
road: The High Pass climbs by caves and rock-gates; a dry shelter in a storm may be a doorway to the dark, and the goblin-gate opens where the path seems safest.
trail: Narrow paths climb from the woods to the wolf-haunted heights; the eagles' road is the wind, and it is not for walking.

forest: Cold pine and spruce on the mountain skirts, dark and resinous, the needled floor muffling every step. Mist pools between the trunks; old boundary-stones and broken walls of lost Arnor surface among the roots.
hill: Stony upland shoulders rising toward the High Pass, grass and lichen over grey rock, strewn with the rubble of old watch-towers and the boundary-marks of a lost realm.
road: A faint remnant of a Dunadan road climbing toward the High Pass, its stones scattered and grass-grown, more memory of a road than a road itself.
trail: A faint upland trace among the pines, marked by cairns half-fallen, that fades into scree near the high places.

forest: Low holly-trees crown the stony hills — Hollin the Elves called this land, for the hollies that were its mark. Their dark leaves catch the sun and their berries glow red as drops of blood on a clear day.
hill: Bare ridges and long slopes of broken stone rise toward the mountain wall. From the high ground the three peaks of Moria stand ahead between the drifting clouds.
road: The old Elven road runs west of the mountains toward the buried doors — grass-grown and rutted now, but its line is still true under the heather, and it ends at the Walls of Moria.
trail: Paths follow the old watercourses toward the mountain's feet; the Sirannon's bed is a thread of brown, red-stained stones, and no bird moves in the empty sky above it.

mountains_low: Barren foothills of red and grey stone, cut by the dry beds of streams that once ran bright. The bones of the great city lie beneath, and the hills keep their counsel.
mountains_med: Three peaks stand over the hidden doors — Caradhras cruel and tall, Celebdil, and Fanuidhol — and below them the Dimrill Dale lies silent around the dark water of Mirrormere.
mountains_high: The horn of Caradhras rises into a world of storm; snow and ice lash its shoulders, and thunder rolls through its hollows when the mountain is angry.
road: The road to the West-gate climbs by the black mere and the last hollies, ending at sheer cliffs and doors that have been shut a thousand years.
trail: Rough tracks cross the Dimrill Dale beside Mirrormere's dark water; the Dimrill Stair climbs the falls beside them, worn by feet that are long gone.

forest: The old forests of Dunland are gone — felled for the fires of Isengard. Stumps and a few bitter brakes remain on the hills; the surviving woods stand far and sparse, and the people remember the trees.
hill: Green hills and long empty downs — a proud, poor country that remembers when it was richer. The hill-men keep their own speech, their own ways, and their old grievances against the strawheads of the valleys.
mountains_low: The foothills of the Misty Mountains rise bare to the west, cut by the gorges of the Isen; the rock is grey and close, and the river runs loud between the walls.
mountains_med: The southern Misty Mountains wall the west — grey heights where the passes of the Gap run up into cloud, and the last peaks look down on the ring of Isengard.
mountains_high: Methedras stands at the range's end — the last horn of the mountains, snow-capped and looking down on the vale of the traitor and the tower that casts a shadow like a hand.
road: The old North-South Road runs down from the Gap of Rohan past the ring of Isengard — once the road of two kingdoms, now a way watched and uneasy, with ruined holdings beside it.
trail: Hill-paths cross the downs to the hidden steads of the Dunlendings; the tracks are many and secret, and the eyes that watch from the ridges are not friendly.

forest: Thin boreal taiga of stunted spruce and pine, lichen-draped and snow-bent, surrendering quickly to open tundra. The trees grow low and hard and the silence is glacial.
hill: Low snow-streaked tundra-hills of bare rock and frozen moss, wind-scoured and treeless under a pale northern sky.
marshes: Frozen fen and bog along the icebound shore, half-marsh half-tundra, meltwater pooling between hummocks of frozen moss where every step is a cold labour.
road: No made road at all; a route across the snow marked by cairns and whale-bone stakes, followed by sled and by foot, that vanishes with each fresh fall.
trail: No trail but a line of footprints soon erased, a route read from the shape of the snow and the set of the wind by those who know the ice.

forest: Scrub and thorn where anything grows at all — grey brambles and stunted bitter trees in the crevices of the Morgai. Nothing green lives long here; the briars claw like wire.
mountains_low: The Morgai — a harsh maze of broken slopes and ravines, sliding scree and jagged ridges, the inner mountain-wall where the last life gives way to bare stone.
road: Broad orc-roads cross the plain, laid straight and dreary between the forts and the furnace-pits; the dust of them hangs in the air and the way is marked by ruin.
trail: Paths climb the ravines of the Morgai by ledges and hidden stairs — ways made for war and watching, hard and bare and cruel.
plains: Gorgoroth — a plateau of ash and slag under a roof of fume. The ground is broken by pits and mounds, the air is bitter and drying, and water is a precious, guarded thing.

forest: The woods thin toward the Morgul Vale — dark ilex and ash, and pale silent groves where the light seems poisoned. Near the Cross-roads the trees stand as if listening for the enemy's drums.
hill: The northern hills are steep and wild, cleft by the black cleft of the Morgul Vale. White pinnacles and broken towers look down on a land that was once all gardens.
road: The wraith-road comes down out of the Vale to meet the Harad Road at the Cross-roads — a pale way between the dead city and the land of shadow. A broken statue of a king keeps watch there, crowned now with trailing flowers.
trail: Stair-paths cut between sheer faces of rock climb the western wall of the Vale — the Straight Stair and the Winding Stair, narrow, cracked by forgotten winters, and watched from above.

forest: A few grey, struggling stands of hardy scrub and dead-looking trees cling to the shores of the bitter inland sea, half-alive under a smoke-stained sky. Little more than the memory of a forest.
marshes: Brackish salt-fens along the Sea of Nurnen, grey and reeking, where slave-worked channels cut through salt-reed and mud under a smoke-stained sky.
mountains_low: The lower volcanic ridges above the Sea of Nurnen, grey-brown and barren but less utterly dead than the north, where slave-fields scrape what little the bitter soil allows.
road: A slave-road of beaten earth along the bitter sea, rutted by the carts that haul Nurn's grudging harvest north to feed the armies of the Dark Tower.
trail: A slave-worn path between the salt-fields and the shore, churned and bitter, watched from the ridges by the overseers.
plains: Grudging grey fields along the bitter sea, salt-crusted and slave-worked, flat and joyless under a smoke-stained sky.

forest: Twisted, tangled woods of the rugged uplands, ancient and deserted: gnarled oak and thorn-brake over broken stony ground, home now only to scattered Druedain and Dunlending bands. A wild, depopulated march where the forest has crept back over abandoned Gondorian land.
hill: Fertile foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with vine and olive and laced with clear streams. Warm and sunlit, the green skirts where mountain meets tilled land.
mountains_low: The green foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with olive and vine where they meet the lowlands, laced with shepherd-paths and tumbling brooks. Warm, fertile and sunlit, the gentlest face of the great range.
mountains_med: The middle slopes of the Ered Nimrais, where forest yields to alpine meadow and grey crag. Cloud snags on the ridges, streams fall in white threads, and the air thins and chills as the green runs out into stone.
mountains_high: The high White Mountains, the Ered Nimrais, crowned with perpetual snow and glacier above the treeline. Knife-edged ridges and sheer pale walls blaze in the sun; the cold is absolute, the silence broken only by wind and distant ice.
road: A well-kept Gondorian road of fitted stone, straight and sure, with drainage and standing waymarks; the traffic of trade and soldiery keeps it busy and its verges clear.
trail: A trodden countryside path between orchards and terraces, sun-warm and clear, worn smooth by shepherds and farmhands.

forest: Cultivated, Mediterranean woodland: groves of holm-oak, chestnut and cypress give way to olive and almond on the warmer slopes, with orchards and flowering vales. The undergrowth is aromatic with broom, thyme and rockrose; tended, sunlit, prosperous woods.
hill: Fertile foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with vine and olive and laced with clear streams. Warm and sunlit, the green skirts where mountain meets tilled land.

hill: Fertile foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with vine and olive and laced with clear streams. Warm and sunlit, the green skirts where mountain meets tilled land.
mountains_low: The green foothills of the White Mountains, terraced with olive and vine where they meet the lowlands, laced with shepherd-paths and tumbling brooks. Warm, fertile and sunlit, the gentlest face of the great range.
mountains_med: The middle slopes of the Ered Nimrais, where forest yields to alpine meadow and grey crag. Cloud snags on the ridges, streams fall in white threads, and the air thins and chills as the green runs out into stone.
mountains_high: The high White Mountains, the Ered Nimrais, crowned with perpetual snow and glacier above the treeline. Knife-edged ridges and sheer pale walls blaze in the sun; the cold is absolute, the silence broken only by wind and distant ice.
road: A well-kept Gondorian road of fitted stone, straight and sure, with drainage and standing waymarks; the traffic of trade and soldiery keeps it busy and its verges clear.
trail: A trodden countryside path between orchards and terraces, sun-warm and clear, worn smooth by shepherds and farmhands.

forest: Pines on the high moors and a tumble of birch, beech and rowan down the steep valley sides; in the hidden valley below, the woods are green and sweet even in late autumn.
hill: The high moor above the valley is bare and windswept heath; the valley itself is a deep-cleft green refuge that the hills conceal from every side.
road: The Road comes down from the moors by steep stony ways, and where the valley is reached it ends — as all journeys here end — at the Last Homely House.
trail: Paths climb between the pines and drop to the ford, where the Bruinen's loud water is the first voice of the valley. Higher up the tracks are for deer and for those who know them.

forest: Thin woods of alder and thorn stand in the wet bottoms, and scrub creeps up the stony ridges. The trees are sparse and old — survivors of a land that was once all farms and fields.
hill: Low rolling hills of tussock and thorn under a wide empty sky. Ruined walls and the grass-grown mounds of old fortifications break the line of the ridges, and the wind has them to itself.
road: The East Road crosses the Lone-lands like a lifeline through wilderness — long straight miles with never a roof nor a wall in sight, and the sky huge overhead.
trail: Sheep-paths and the sunken lines of older ways wander the hills, fading into heather and bog where the land was once all tilled.

forest: Fangorn — the last great wood of the Elder Days, deep-tangled and vast. The forest floor is buried under drifts of leaves; the air beneath the boughs is stifling and strangely thin, and the trees are watchful. Some are more than trees, and the wood is not empty of shepherds.
road: No road enters Fangorn — the Entwash skirts it and the old ways die at the eaves. Within there are only the paths the forest permits, and they are not made for wheels.
trail: Paths wind under the high boughs between halls of still trees; climbing north they reach bare slopes where gaunt pines stand alone, and a sharp white mountain peak shows beyond the far valley.

forest: A sickened wood of strangled oak and webbed beech, lightless and rank, where the canopy mats out the sky and the very ground feels diseased. The dread of the Necromancer's hill seeps through every shadow.
road: A furtive orc-track beaten through the sick forest, muddy and root-choked, marked here and there by grisly totems; no honest road, only a way the enemy's servants use.
trail: A furtive game-path through the strangled trees, slick with black mud and webbed overhead, that seems to lead the walker deeper against his will.

forest: The Golden Wood — mallorn-trees with bark of silver-grey whose leaves turn gold and do not fall until spring. Beneath them the grass is long and green, and the light under the boughs is like the light of evening that never ends.
road: No road for wheels runs in Lórien; the ways are the paths of the Elves, winding under the mallorn boughs to the hidden bridges of the streams and the green mound at the wood's heart.
trail: Paths climb by Nimrodel's bright water into the heart of the wood, and up through the double ring of trees to Cerin Amroth, where the grass is starred with elanor and niphredil.

forest: Scattered copses of oak, elm and hazel stand among the fields, and the woody slopes of the Green Hills carry birch and fir. Their shade is kindly; on quiet nights mist rises from the streams between the roots.
hill: Rolling green hills stitched with hedgerows, where hobbit-holes burrow into the sheltered slopes. From the crests the patchwork of fields, lanes and water-meadows spreads out on every side.
marshes: Wet meadows and reedy margins lie along the Water and the streams of the Marish, soft underfoot after rain; the rushes whisper where the ditches run full.
road: The Great East Road runs through on its ancient line — a broad way of packed earth between hedgerows. Lesser lanes wander between field-gates, mill-ponds and the round doors of the hillsides.
trail: Narrow trodden paths cut across the pasture and between the drystone walls — ways used more by hobbits and their carts than by any stranger.

forest: The Chetwood covers the northern slopes — a quiet wood of oak and beech long thinned for timber and charcoal. Beyond its eaves the land is bare hedged country and open field.
hill: Bree Hill rises green and steep above the village, crowned with the dike and deep hedge that ring the settlement. Its flanks are pasture and garden-ground; eastward the land falls away toward wild and empty country.
marshes: East of the village the Midgewater Marshes spread flat and cheerless — pools and reed-beds under a wide sky, loud with hidden birds and the whining of midges. No road crosses them; the wet and the biting things are the only tenants.
road: Two ancient ways cross at the village gate: the Great East Road running on toward the Misty Mountains, and the old Greenway grass-grown and dwindling north into the empty lands.
trail: Field-paths and cart-ruts join the outlying farms of Staddle and Archet to the gate. After dark the lanes are empty and the watchman's lantern marks the village edge.

forest: Warm, dry woodland of cork-oak, pine and terebinth on sun-baked hillsides, edged by the famous vineyards of the Wineland. The light is hard and bright, the shade sparse and resin-scented, on the eastern edge of the maps.
road: A dusty cart-road between the vineyards and river-wharves, warm and well-travelled, rich with the traffic of the wine-trade toward the east.
trail: A warm path between the vine-rows, trodden by pickers, dusty and sweet with the smell of ripening grapes.
